name: Mescio Insights
author: Mescio

sections.description:
Mescio Insights is the observability layer for the Mescio stack.

  • Mescio for Agents makes the site readable (Markdown, llms.txt).
  • WebMCP Bridge makes it usable (search, retrieve, cart, MCP tools).
  • Mescio Insights shows whether those layers were actually requested.

It listens to the shared mescio_agent_request hook. You can run Insights with Mescio only, WebMCP only, or both.

What you get

  • Hits by channel (markdown, llms, rest, mcp, webmcp)
  • Hits by client (GPTBot, Claude, ChatGPT, … — from the User-Agent, not from ChatGPT citations)
  • Last request, unique clients, hour-of-day
  • Daily bars, filters, pagination
  • CSV export
  • First open copies an existing Mescio Agent activity log
  • Optional public summary: shortcode [mescio_insights] and REST /wp-json/mescio-insights/v1/summary (counts only, off by default)
  • Retention 7–90 days
  • No IP addresses, no request bodies, nothing sent off-site

What this is not

A ChatGPT ranking score. A GEO API product. A hosted portal. Those may come later as a separate module.

Requirements

WordPress 6.0+ and at least one of:

  • Mescio for Agents 1.8.0+
  • WebMCP Bridge 1.10.1+ (trunk that always fires mescio_agent_request)
sections.installation:
1. Copy the mescio-insights folder into wp-content/plugins/
  2. Activate Mescio Insights
  3. Open Mescio Insights in the admin menu
  4. Keep Mescio and/or WebMCP active so events are emitted
sections.faq:
Does this replace Agent activity in Mescio?

No. Mescio 1.8 still has a short local log. Insights is the fuller dashboard and keeps its own table.

Will you see my data?

No. Rows stay in your WordPress database.

Can I show this on the public site?

Yes, after you enable Public summary under Log settings. Use the shortcode [mescio_insights] or [mescio_insights days="7"]. It prints counts, channels and client names — not paths, not user-agent strings, not IP addresses.

Why is the log empty with only WebMCP 1.10.1 from WordPress.org?

1.10.1 only fires the hook if something is already listening. Insights registers a listener, so current trunk of WebMCP (and Insights + Mescio together) is enough. A future WebMCP tag always emits the hook.

1.2.1

  • Read after last edit: per page and bot, whether the last fetch was after you saved the post
  • OpenAI/Anthropic labels include purpose (training, index, live query)
  • Last-visit charts stay; this table answers a different question

1.2.0

  • Lighter admin screen (no hero photo or paper texture)
  • Menu label is Mescio Insights
  • First visit copies the Mescio Agent activity log when Insights is empty
  • Extra metrics: last request, unique clients, hour of day
  • Optional public summary shortcode and REST route (off by default)

1.1.3

  • Hide unrelated theme/plugin notices on the Insights screen
  • Explain the empty log and how to record the first hit

1.1.2

1.1.1
